canonical_claim: `CaGcShardIncarnationCore.tla` checks `INV_NO_DANGLING` and `INV_NO_ORPHAN_EDGE` across 724,944 distinct states and proves that two orthogonal coordinates (a durable never-reused `incarnation` stamped at shard creation, and the pool-global GC `round`) are both necessary; three negative controls (`SabotageNewbornNoFloor`, `SabotagePathKeyedCursor`, `SabotageDeleteBeforeFold`) each show a counterexample when one coordinate is removed.; The core invariants (INV-NO-LOSS, INV-NO-DANGLE, INV-NO-RETURN, INV-JOURNAL-COVERAGE, MonotoneGC) are model-checked by CaIncarnationCore.tla; mount-safety invariants (WriterEpochMonotoneUnique, SupersededWriterMakesNoMutation) are model-checked by a focused Phase-0 TLA+ model; INV-NO-DANGLING and INV-NO-ORPHAN-EDGE under D1 are model-checked by CaGcShardIncarnationCore.tla (724,944 states, GREEN as of 2026-07-01).

The planned parallel commit snapshots parts into an index-addressable vector, preallocates outcome and exception slots, dispatches bounded worker loops, waits with `wait()` rather than `get()`, and performs rollback only after the inner runner scope drains.
A `Live` catalog row is safe only when its life's `_ckpt` exists; this protects against both an over-broad janitor and a fenced or token-stale creator installing late.

A frontier-probe budget suppressor must be pinned by deleting the namespace `_ckpt`, hiding its prefix, and asserting `frontier_unprobed_budget > 0`; leaving `_ckpt` in place allows the namespace to be proven without consuming the budget.
The modeled `EarnedFarewell` invariant permits farewell only after a provable drain, and `OneWay` forbids transitions from `IdentityLost` or `Vanished` back to `Live` or `Transient`.
`CaB140DangleMerge` passed its empty-`Trees` configuration `m_empty_trees.cfg` as green.

The confirm model proves custody-chain safety under the explicitly named assumption `CommittedEdgesAreGcVisible`; the sender certificate and GC contract are layered, with GC turning the certified binding into blob liveness.
A `NamespaceLifeId` may originate only from catalog snapshot resolution; it must never be minted from a `RootNamespace`, LIST key, or path.

The `checkpoint_unusable` frontier bucket counts only the no-cursor variant; when an unreadable checkpoint has a cursor, the effective-hold site overwrites the reason with `Held`, while the warning and seal still retain the underlying `CheckpointUndecodable` cause.

Under the one-pipeline transaction design, CA manifest build, blob upload, and promote (remote I/O) deliberately run inside `MergeTreeData::Transaction::commit` under `lockParts()` (`MergeTreeData.cpp:8775/8792`); this is an accepted tradeoff per the spec's `Why There Is No Disk Precommit` rationale, not a regression, since moving remote I/O out of `data_parts` locking is a general commit-positioning/performance problem, not a CA-only correctness issue.

The "natural black-box equivalence" test oracle requires a CA table to be byte-for-byte identical to a normal MergeTree table on the same data under active GC (stateless tests 04278/04279); divergence means a live blob was lost.

On existing non-CAS disks, immediate local-filesystem visibility and object-storage parts represented as independent files generally prevented the weak disk-transaction contract from causing direct data loss, but MergeTree still depended on implementation-specific visibility and early sub-part commits.

An external author review of rev.6 confirmed 3 substantive findings: F1 seal-skip-on-empty-dead-region combined with a blind detector, F2 a sticky-boundary-bool causing over-seal plus a fail-open allowlist, and F3 the seal PUT held under `state_mutex` for up to 90s; all three were filed as a fix-round task.
The dead-precommit skip was not the S42 cause because `dead_precommits_skipped` was zero on both nodes; the skipped `-1` path never fired.
v2 gates compatibility_version on the raw preamble before parsing any body bytes, so a future object reports UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION rather than a parse error

`dropNamespace(const NamespaceLifeId &)` rejects a stale held incarnation through the `expected_incarnation` guard and throws a retry-later exception instead of writing against a successor namespace life. Additionally, The only life-taking mutation entry point is `dropNamespace(const NamespaceLifeId &)`, and its stale-incarnation guard ensures a held life can never target a reborn successor namespace. Additionally, A stale-life `store->dropNamespace(life1)` after life 2 is admitted throws `ErrorCodes::NETWORK_ERROR`, leaves the catalog token and bytes unchanged, and does not prevent an independent fresh store from resolving life 2.

With both namespaces truthfully grounded in the list-liar fixture, `frontier_namespaces = 2 > 0` and `universe_authoritative = true` under `UniversePolicy::kDefault` (`= Authoritative`), so those terms cannot make this fixture's `frontier_complete` false.
Phase A removes the writer fence-round refresh only when its TLA+ newborn-shard gate confirms the redundancy; the GC-side fence_round remains.

The recommended transient-classifier fix is to add `throwCasTransientUnavailable` beside `throwCasWriteRetryLater` in `Backend/CasRequestControl.cpp:190-201`, minting `NETWORK_ERROR` for `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage.cpp:1111`, `:1163`, and `CasMountRuntime.cpp:106`; this changes no upstream files.

The shipped E3 replay optimization applies `TrustedHistory` in place with no copy and accepts a poisoned local state on throw because replay returns the state only after full success; `Full` retains the two-phase scratch-copy guarantee.
